From: Samir Rao <samir@searchly.ai>

Date: 2026-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Embeddings rate & model compatibility question

Hi Connor,

We’re evaluating Redwood for our vector store and had a few quick questions on embeddings pricing and model support before scheduling a demo. We're primarily interested in hosted API pricing for embeddings.

1) Do you price embeddings per-vector or per-token? If per-vector, how do you handle different dimensions (e.g., 1536 vs 768 vs 4096) — is there a dimension multiplier or separate SKUs?
2) Which embedding models are supported today (and recommended for semantic search) — any differences in cost for sema-3-large vs sema-3-small or open variants?
3) Do quantized/compact embeddings (lower-d precision) affect pricing or eligibility for certain tiers?
4) What discounts or bulk-pack structures do you offer for committed volumes (we're looking at ~50M vectors/month initial, and a potential 500M vectors/year plan)? Any minimums or usage commit periods?
5) Any constraints on embedding throughput (rps) at those volumes for hosted API and recommended Dedicated options?

Can you share a baseline ratecard or a quick quote with example numbers? Prefer a per-month/monthly cost example for 50M vectors at 1536 dims and second example for the annual 500M vectors.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Best,
Samir Rao
Head of Search
Searchly Inc.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Embeddings rate & model compatibility question

Hi Samir — thanks for the detailed note and the volume context, that's really helpful.

Short answers up front: we price embeddings as per-vector units for hosted API, with an explicit mapping from model/dimension to a per-vector unit cost (so higher-dim models map to more units). Quantized embeddings don’t change the billing unit but we do have guidance on quality/compatibility for compact formats.

A couple clarifying quick questions so we can give an apples-to-apples quote:
- Are the 50M vectors/month coming from short text (<= 512 chars) or longer documents? This affects tokenization and preprocessing costs.
- What’s the expected QPS for embedding requests (steady vs spiky)?
- Do you require exportable vectors (S3/Download) or real-time-only serving?

I can put together a worked example (50M monthly and 500M annual) and a couple of pack/commit options — would you prefer a spreadsheet or a short PDF? If you're free, I can also schedule a 30-min call with our pricing lead.

Talk soon,

Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Connor / Marissa — see pricing options below. I’ll attach the detailed spreadsheet and a one-pager you can send to Searchly.

Executive summary (hosted API, billed per-vector unit):

Option A — Pay-as-you-go (no commit)
- Baseline: $0.000016 per-vector (1536-d model = 1 unit)
- 768-d model mapped to 0.55 units (rounded) => effective $0.0000088/vector
- 4096-d model mapped to 2.6 units => effective $0.0000416/vector
- Notes: no minimum, standard 30-day billing

Option B — 1-year commitment
- 10% off baseline per-vector rates for annual 1-year commit >= 100M vectors
- Volume tiers for deeper discount: 10–100M: 10% | 100–500M: 18% | >500M: 25%
- Includes S3 export (monthly) at no additional charge for first 1TB; overage billed at $0.05/GB

Option C — Enterprise License Agreement (3-year)
- Custom pricing with guarantee of throughput SLOs; typical pricing ranges -25% to -40% off baseline depending on commit and SLAs
- Dedicated deployment option available (reserved capacity) with separate reserved compute fees + reduced per-vector bill

Model support & cost notes:
- Supported/Recommended: redwood-emb-1536, redwood-emb-768, sema-3-large, sema-3-small. We maintain compatibility matrices in the console.
- Billing is per-vector unit as described; dimension multiplier is used to normalize across SKUs — not per-token.
- Quantized embeddings: billing unchanged; however quality/compatibility can vary — we offer an eval run and a small free trial for sample datasets.

Throughput/Capacity:
- Hosted API can support 2.5k rps sustained with autoscaling for short-term spikes; for steady >3k rps or strict latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity.

Next steps:
- I’ll attach the spreadsheet (Embeddings_Pricing_Options_Q2_2026.pdf and Redwood_Embeddings_Ratecard_Summary.xlsx). Please review; I suggest we send the one-pager to Samir and include the spreadsheet. If they want a firm enterprise quote, we can open an RFQ and draft an SOW.

Pricing negotiation playbook:
- Use volume tiers and commit length to justify deeper discounts. Avoid discounts >35% without legal approval and finance sign-off.
- Consider offering a one-time onboarding credit for export costs.

Laura Bennett
Director, Pricing
Redwood Inference
